# Why Databrary? {.unnumbered}

Data repositories and libraries provide permanent homes for research findings and raw data. Sharing research data is a vital component of the research process, just like publishing papers and books, giving talks, and teaching classes. Open science and sharing information is how we advance as a community.

Many granting agencies require that research data be shared. As an NIH-approved repository, Databrary provides NIH grantees with a compliant and streamlined way to fulfill their data-sharing obligations.

Videos are expensive and time consuming to collect and annotate. Sharing and reusing videos accelerates discovery. Researchers across fields can reuse video data and glean insights beyond those of the original data contributor.

## Our Framework

Databrary is structured on a framework of open sharing with restricted access. Open sharing on Databrary allows researchers to reuse data without contacting the original data contributor. However, access to Databrary is restricted to authorized investigators who have completed the formal agreement between the researcher's institution and New York University, the host institution for Databrary. The formal agreement states that the researcher is affiliated with their institution and that the institution will be responsible for the researcher's relationship with Databrary.

This framework aims to advance the widespread sharing of research data while respecting the privacy of research participants.

We encourage you to read [Databrary's Access Agreement](https://databrary.org/about/agreement/agreement). The agreement provides information about how Databrary is structured and how it should be used. You should get guidance from your institution's research ethics board (IRB) for reusing data for research purposes.
